scenes.line1: Why do we use the test pyramid?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why we stack more unit tests than integration or end-to-end tests? Let’s break down the test pyramid and its trade-offs.

scenes.label: Unit
scenes.sub: Fast, cheap, and easy to maintain.
scenes.say: Unit tests are your foundation. They’re fast, cheap, and easy to maintain.
Integration tests check how parts work together, but they’re slower and more complex. End-to-end tests cover real user flows, but they’re the slowest and most fragile.
A solid pyramid might have a hundred unit tests, twenty integration tests, and just five end-to-end tests.

scenes.question: Should you maximize E2E tests for coverage?
scenes.wrong: Yes, more E2E tests means better coverage.
scenes.right: No, too many E2E tests slow you down and increase maintenance. Balance test types for reliability and speed.
scenes.say: Here’s a common interview trap: Should you maximize end-to-end tests for coverage? Actually, too many slows you down and makes maintenance harder. Balance is key.
